newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SIDHU CENTURY GIVES INDIA UPPER HAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SIDHU CENTURY GIVES INDIA UPPER HAND.

text.p: Navjot Sidhu hit an unbeaten century on Saturday to guide India to a strong position at tea on the opening day of the first test against Sri Lanka.
The in-form opener was on 103 as India reached tea at 174 for one.

Rahul Dravid gave solid support with a patient knock of 58 in three hours as the second wicket pair put together a stand of 138. That followed the loss of Nayan Mongia, caught at third slip for seven.
After that success for Ravindra Pushpakumara, Sri Lanka's bowlers toiled without reward on a slow, deadpan wicket.

Sidhu, driving with confidence, reached his eighth test century in 220 minutes off 171 balls, hitting two sixes and 12 fours. It was his second successive century of the tour following the unbeaten 100 he scored in the three-day match against a Sri Lanka Board XI three days ago.
Dravid completed his ninth test half-century shortly before the break, facing 149 balls and hitting seven fours.
